candidate_relations.reason: A hard mobile yellowish tonsillar lesion with ovoid calcification is a stone, not lymphoma, and there is no lymphadenopathy.
Odynophagia is the presenting symptom after perceived foreign body, not the tonsillolith itself.
The lesion is a benign tonsillar finding but the required object is a tonsillolith, not a nonspecific benign lesion.
Uniform ovoid calcification without ulceration or systemic TB features is not tuberculosis of the tonsil.
The radiograph shows dystrophic calcification in the tonsillar region, which is the mechanism of a tonsillolith but not the named diagnosis.
Tonsillolithiasis is a wording variant of tonsillolith, matching the hard yellowish tonsillar calculus on exam and radiograph.
Tobacco use is noted, but the discrete calcified tonsillar protrusion is not a tobacco-related mucosal lesion.
No ulceration, mass elsewhere, or lymphadenopathy; the lesion is hard, mobile, and calcified, unlike squamous carcinoma.
A uniformly calcified ovoid tonsillar body is not a dermoid cyst.
The calcification overlies the tonsillar fossa, not a tooth surface, so dental calculus is a different object.
No fish bone was seen; the radiograph showed tonsillar calcification instead, so fish-bone impaction is the incompatible initial impression.
Betel-nut chewing is a risk factor for other oral lesions, not for this discrete calcified tonsillolith.
Tonsillar calcinosis names the same calcified tonsillar concretion documented clinically and radiographically.
There are no TB signs; the finding is an isolated tonsillar calcification.
The lesion is hard and radiopaque, not a fluid-filled tonsillar cyst.
Tonsillolith is the reference diagnosis and matches the yellowish hard tonsillar calculus with ovoid calcification.
The lesion is nontender, well-delineated, and calcified without fluctuance, unlike tonsillar abscess.
An osteoma is a bony neoplasm, not a mobile tonsillar concretion.
Flexible endoscopy and radiograph excluded a retained foreign body in favor of intrinsic tonsillar calcification.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: retained foreign body vs intrinsic tonsillar stone

candidate_relations.reason: No mucosal ulceration or invasive mass; the calcified mobile lesion is not tonsillar squamous carcinoma.
